subject.title: fix(mcp): keep servers whose tool schemas omit a root type

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally tolerate MCP tool schemas that omit the protocol/SDK-required root `type: "object"`, or should affected servers be required to emit the standard root-object shape while an upstream SDK capability is pursued?
rationale: The change is not only a parser repair: it creates a compatibility extension beyond the dependency contract, and the available fallback cannot preserve SDK-private metadata without choosing a supported integration boundary.

options.title: Keep the protocol boundary
options.body: Reject omitted-root schemas as today and ask the MCP server or SDK project to provide a compliant or supported fix.

options.title: Support a narrow compatibility extension
options.body: Accept only demonstrated input schemas after adding or obtaining an SDK-supported tolerant parse path that also initializes normal tool metadata.

options.title: Accept both input and output extensions
options.body: Expand the compatibility policy only with explicit downstream validation and metadata behavior for output schemas.

recommendation.title: Keep the protocol boundary
recommendation.body: Reject omitted-root schemas as today and ask the MCP server or SDK project to provide a compliant or supported fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main MCP feature ownership requires the unavailable repository-history inspection; this choice belongs with the owner of the MCP runtime boundary.
